scenario: A property / REIT company has made secured development and project loans. The auditor wants to identify the relevant IFRS 9 ECL requirements and comparable public-company disclosures.
expected_authority_behaviour: Retrieve applicable existing official authority cards.
Keep official requirements separate from company disclosures.
expected_comparator_behaviour: Perform comparable-company research within existing supported evidence boundaries.
Assess property-development business and loan exposure, not generic ECL terminology.
expected_stop_or_handoff_behaviour: Finish with auditor judgement and further review required.
notes: Property-development-loan flagship; no company is named in the scenario.

scenario: An e-commerce company has material trade receivables from merchants and customers. The auditor wants to understand the relevant IFRS 9 impairment requirements and comparable disclosures.
expected_authority_behaviour: Identify that simplified-approach authority may be required.
If the curated registry is insufficient, explicitly record an authority gap rather than inventing requirements or paragraph references.
expected_comparator_behaviour: Comparable disclosure research may proceed only within supported evidence boundaries.
Assess trade-receivable and e-commerce exposure comparability.
expected_stop_or_handoff_behaviour: Retain auditor review and any unresolved official-authority gap.
notes: An authority gap is a valid safe outcome; unsupported extrapolation is not.

scenario: A manufacturing company has a large portfolio of trade receivables. Overdue balances have increased and several major customers account for a significant share of the balance. The auditor wants to research the applicable IFRS 9 ECL requirements and how comparable manufacturers incorporate historical loss experience and forward-looking information into their disclosures.
expected_research_topics: historical loss experience or provision-matrix considerations
customer concentration and delinquency as relevant credit-risk information
expected_authority_behaviour: Use existing official authority where covered.
Seek sufficient official authority for trade-receivable simplified-approach / lifetime-ECL and historical-loss or provision-matrix considerations; surface insufficient coverage.
Do not require SICR tracking as though the general approach necessarily applies.
Make no unsupported requirements or paragraph-reference claims.
expected_comparator_behaviour: Assess industry and exposure comparability rather than matching generic ECL terminology.
notes: Customer concentration and overdue balances are scenario facts, not proof of a particular accounting treatment.

scenario: A bank has a loan portfolio for which credit risk may have increased significantly since initial recognition. The auditor wants to research the relevant IFRS 9 requirements and comparable banking disclosures.
expected_authority_behaviour: Retrieve applicable official authority where covered.
expected_comparator_behaviour: Banking issuers may be appropriate comparators.
Unrelated property issuers must not be rated strong merely because they mention ECL.
expected_stop_or_handoff_behaviour: Finish with auditor review and supported comparator limitations.
notes: Framework compatibility alone does not establish economic comparability.

scenario: A corporate treasury function holds debt investments measured at amortised cost and the auditor wants to understand the applicable IFRS 9 impairment requirements and comparable disclosures.
expected_authority_behaviour: Recognise the relevant impairment research scope.
expected_comparator_behaviour: Distinguish debt investments from trade receivables and development loans.
expected_stop_or_handoff_behaviour: Retain human review and unresolved evidence limitations.
notes: Do not treat generic receivable or development-loan disclosures as an established investment comparator.

scenario: A property-management company has material lease receivables and the auditor wants to understand the applicable expected-credit-loss requirements and comparable disclosures.
expected_authority_behaviour: Identify the relevant IFRS 9 simplified-approach / lifetime-ECL accounting-policy election for lease receivables; do not imply that the simplified approach is automatically mandatory for all lease receivables.
Seek sufficient official authority before concluding how that policy election applies.
Surface insufficient official coverage instead of extrapolating development-loan treatment.
expected_comparator_behaviour: Assess lease-receivable exposure comparability within supported evidence boundaries.
expected_stop_or_handoff_behaviour: Retain the authority gap and auditor review when coverage is insufficient.
notes: Property-management business terminology does not establish development-loan equivalence.

scenario: A company has issued financial guarantees and undrawn loan commitments and the auditor wants to understand whether and how expected-credit-loss requirements apply.
expected_authority_behaviour: If the existing registry is insufficient, request additional official authority or abstain from a requirements conclusion.
expected_stop_or_handoff_behaviour: Explicitly request additional official authority or abstain when required; retain auditor review.

scenario: The auditor of an e-commerce company wants to know which accounting requirements govern revenue recognition and whether comparable listed-company disclosures are available.
expected_research_topics: different accounting-standard research scope for revenue recognition
expected_authority_behaviour: Identify that this is not an IFRS 9 impairment research question.
expected_comparator_behaviour: Do not run irrelevant ECL comparator research.
expected_stop_or_handoff_behaviour: State that a different accounting-standard research scope is required; do not force the scenario into the IFRS 9 ECL workflow.
